title: Lint --fix through the compile gate
summary: lint --fix --apply --project X.dproj --compile-gate writes the fixes only if the project still builds; a fix that breaks the compile is refused and rolled back
intro: Read this before letting lint --fix write into a project you cannot afford to break. With --compile-gate the project builds before and after the write and any compile error rolls every file back. Opt-in: without the flag nothing builds, except a naming rename (field/param/local/const prefix or casing fixes), which is always written through the gate when --project names a .dproj.

help:
drag-lint lint --in --fix [--fix-line --fix-rule ] [--fix-naming] [--apply [--no-backup]] [--project --compile-gate [--platform

] [--rsvars ] [--build-timeout ]] (AUTOFIX one file; --apply keeps a .bak beside each file it writes unless --no-backup)

questions.ask: How do I make lint --fix check that the project still builds?
Why did lint --fix --apply refuse my fix?
